notes: If name is omitted, a random human-readable name is generated automatically
The worktree name will be used as the branch name
Gitignored files matching .worktreeinclude at the checkout root are copied into the new worktree
.worktreeinclude and --copy-file use gitignore syntax. A file is copied only when it matches and is gitignored, so tracked files are never duplicated
Files that already exist in the new worktree are left unchanged
Symlinks are skipped and are not followed. A .worktreeinclude symlink is not read

preferences.name: preferences

examples.description: Store a custom worktrees directory (relative to the Git repository root) for all commands
Store a separator for flattening worktree directory names while keeping branch names unchanged
Keep branches by default when deleting worktrees with ptm delete
Disable automatic project discovery through ghq
Store repositories cloned by ptm clone under ~/ghq

notes: Subcommands:
get <key>    Show a preference value
set <key>    Set a preference value
remove <key> Remove a preference value
Preferences are stored in $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/ptm/config.toml (default ~/.config/ptm/config.toml).
The file and directory are created on the first set. Comments and formatting are preserved.
Supported keys:
worktrees-directory - path relative to the Git repo root for storing worktrees (defaults to .git/ptm/worktrees)
directory-name-separator - replaces '/' in worktree directory names only (defaults to / for nested directories)
keep-branch - keeps the branch when deleting a worktree (defaults to false)
ghq-discovery - discovers ghq-managed repositories as projects (defaults to true)
root - absolute path, or ~/path, where ptm clone places repositories (defaults to the first git config ghq.root, then $GHQ_ROOT, then ~/ghq)

preferences get.name: preferences get

examples.description: Show the preferred worktrees directory (relative to repo root)
Show the preferred worktree directory name separator

notes: Supported keys: worktrees-directory, directory-name-separator, keep-branch, ghq-discovery, root

preferences set.name: preferences set

examples.description: Store worktrees in ../phantom-worktrees relative to the Git repository root
Flatten worktree directory names such as feature/test to feature-test
Keep branches when deleting worktrees by default
Disable automatic project discovery through ghq

notes: Supported keys: worktrees-directory, directory-name-separator, keep-branch, ghq-discovery, root
For worktrees-directory, provide a path relative to the Git repository root; defaults to .git/ptm/worktrees when unset
For directory-name-separator, '/' keeps nested directories; any other string replaces '/' only in the directory path
For keep-branch, use true to preserve branches on delete or false to keep the default branch deletion behavior
For ghq-discovery, use false to list only projects registered directly with ptm
For root, provide an absolute path or a path starting with ~/. ptm clone uses it as the repository root
keep-branch and ghq-discovery are stored as TOML booleans. The other keys are strings.

clone.name: clone
clone.description: Clone a Git repository into the ghq-compatible layout and register it

options.name: branch
options.description: Branch to check out when the repository is cloned

options.name: depth
options.description: Create a shallow clone with this many commits. Must be a positive integer

options.name: update
options.description: Fetch origin when the repository already exists at the destination

options.name: json
options.description: Print a versioned JSON object to stdout. Git progress goes to stderr. Errors use the version 1 error object

examples.description: Clone owner/repo from github.com
Clone an SSH URL and check out a branch
Shallow clone and print the versioned JSON result
Fetch an existing checkout and register it

notes: owner/repo uses github.com. host/owner/repo uses that host.
https URLs, http URLs, ssh:// URLs, and scp-style git@host:owner/repo paths are accepted. A trailing .git suffix is optional.
The repository is placed at <root>/<host>/<owner>/<repo>. The host is lowercased, and a URL port is part of that directory (example.net:9443).

The root is the root key in $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/ptm/config.toml, otherwise the first git config ghq.root value, otherwise $GHQ_ROOT, otherwise ~/ghq. A configured root is used without reading git config. A git config read failure warns and falls through to $GHQ_ROOT or ~/ghq.
When that path is already the same repository root, ptm registers it and prints the path instead of cloning again. --update fetches origin in that case.
remoteUrl omits http and https userinfo, including a token used as the username. ssh and scp-style URLs keep the login name. file:// URLs and absolute scp-style paths are rejected.
--branch and --depth apply only when cloning. updated is true only when an existing repository was fetched.
If the path exists but is not that repository, the command exits with a validation error.
The project is always registered. Worktrees still live under the repository's .git/ptm/worktrees directory.
Authentication is left to Git. ptm does not call gh.
Git progress is written to stderr. With --json, stdout is only the version 1 result: path, host, owner, repo, remoteUrl, cloned, and updated.
